questions.question: When should you always signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you are doing and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield.
Crossroad ahead.
Keep right.
Yield ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: Three-sided signs tell you to slow down at an intersection. Be ready to stop and let other drivers or pedestrians go first. You can drive when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Drive around any lowered gates.
Assume no train is coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing signs warn you that a train might be near. Always obey railroad crossing signs. Never drive around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your freeway exit?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next exit.
questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Do not stop on the highway, back up, swerve suddenly to make an exit, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop before entering.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic in the intersection or roadway go first.

questions.question: When should you never pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or around a curve.
When a school bus has flashing lights.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass on a hill or curve where you cannot see oncoming traffic, at an intersection, on a railroad crossing or bridge, or in any no passing zone. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: How can you make sure your health does not affect your driving safety?

options.text: Stay in good physical shape and get regular checkups.
Know how medicine affects your driving.
Drive only when you feel well.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Your health is important for safe driving. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe. Stay fit, get regular checkups, and understand how medicine might affect you.

questions.question: When a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow their directions instead of the traffic light. Police officers control traffic to keep it moving safely and prevent crashes.

questions.question: You see or hear an emergency vehicle on a divided highway. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore it if other lanes are available.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down, move over, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move over, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren, slow down, move your car to make a clear path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What is important to remember about trucks on the road?

options.text: They need more distance to stop than cars do.
They can pass faster going downhill than cars.
They turn with a smaller radius than cars.
They can pass faster going uphill than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more distance to stop than cars do.
questions.explanation: Trucks are heavy and large. Because of their size and weight, trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, who must you yield to?

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, slow down and let pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout go first.

questions.question: Is drinking alcohol and driving a safety problem?

options.text: No, it is a minor problem.
Yes, it is a serious problem.
No, it is safe with just a few drinks.
It only affects the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a serious problem.
questions.explanation: Drinking and driving is a serious safety problem. Safe driving is impossible when you drink alcohol or use drugs. Impaired driving is dangerous to you and everyone on the road.

questions.question: If you feel too sleepy to drive safely, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road and rest.
Drink a large energy drink.
Open all windows and turn on the air conditioning.
Talk to a friend on the phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and rest.
questions.explanation: When you are tired, you cannot drive safely. Your reactions slow down and your decisions become poor. On long drives, take a break every two hours. If you feel drowsy, leave the road and rest.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Let time pass so your body can remove the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let time pass so your body can remove the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not reduce your BAC or make you sober. They might keep you awake, but they do not change how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at other vehicles.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers. Move your car as far off the road as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your car is broken.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against their red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and drive past the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always give pedestrians the right of way. Even if you have a green light, stop if pedestrians are in the intersection. Be careful around pedestrians at all times.

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You are making a turn.
Your emergency brake is on.
You are changing lanes.
You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working at all times when you drive.

questions.question: If you have the right-of-way at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Assume all other drivers will follow the rules.
Wave other drivers forward before you go.
Drive through immediately.
Look for other cars, pedestrians, and bicycles before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for other cars, pedestrians, and bicycles before moving forward.
questions.explanation: After you stop at an intersection, look carefully before moving. Check left, right, and left again for traffic and bicycles before entering the intersection.

questions.question: Before you turn, change lanes, or leave a curb, you must signal. This is:

options.text: Only necessary if other cars are around.
A good habit and required by law.
Only necessary during the move, not before.
Not necessary if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good habit and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn or change lanes. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving your car right or left. Always signal before leaving a curb.

questions.question: Who must wear a fastened safety belt in a moving vehicle?

options.text: The driver
Front seat passengers
Children ages 8 to 18
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: The law requires the driver and front seat passengers to wear safety belts. All children ages 8 to 18 must also wear safety belts, no matter where they sit in the car.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Stay farther back from the car ahead.
Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see. Take steps to make driving safer for you and other drivers on the road.

questions.question: When are seat belts most effective?

options.text: Only for the driver.
For passengers on long drives.
For everyone on a highway.
For everyone in the car every time it is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: For everyone in the car every time it is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your car should wear a seat belt every time you drive. In a crash, a person without a seat belt can become a danger to others in the car.

questions.question: What must you do with traffic signs and pavement markings?

options.text: Always obey them.
They are just suggestions.
Follow them only when other cars are present.
Follow them only when a police officer is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always obey them.
questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow. They tell you about road conditions and help you drive safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: The driver ahead is using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Give that car extra space.
Know that driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Do not drive the same way.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. Keep your eyes on the road. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because they are more likely to crash.
